glossary.Microvascular: Affecting the smallest blood vessels, such as retinal capillaries.
glossary.Retina: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.
glossary.Glycaemic control: How well blood glucose is kept in the target range.
glossary.Exudates: Yellow deposits of leaked lipid and protein in the retina.
glossary.Retinal infarction: Death of a small area of retina from blocked blood supply, seen as cotton wool spots.
glossary.Venous looping: Veins that loop back on themselves, a sign of retinal ischaemia.
glossary.Fibrovascular proliferation: Growth of scar tissue with new vessels that can pull on and detach the retina.
glossary.Opacity: Something that blocks light passing through, here blood in the vitreous.
glossary.Fundal: Relating to the fundus, the back of the eye seen through the pupil.
glossary.Fundus: The inside back surface of the eye, including retina, optic disc and macula.
glossary.Clinically significant: Enough to matter for treatment or vision.
glossary.Conservatively: Without active procedures, by monitoring and modifying risk factors.
glossary.Pre-proliferative: The stage before new vessel growth, similar to severe NPDR.
glossary.Night vision: Seeing in dim light, often reduced after pan-retinal laser.
glossary.Peripheral field loss: Loss of the outer parts of the visual field.
glossary.VEGF inhibitors: Drugs that block vascular endothelial growth factor, stopping leaky new vessel growth.
glossary.Capillary occlusion: Blockage of the smallest blood vessels.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.Pathological: Caused by or relating to disease.
glossary.Permeability: How easily fluid and protein leak through vessel walls.
glossary.Photocoagulation: Using a laser to burn and seal retinal tissue.
